transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because my eating has gotten really messed up. I just stopped caring about tracking food, and then I wasn’t really eating proper meals for days—mostly coffee and protein bars. My clothes started getting loose before I even really noticed what was happening.
Have you had any episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short time, or done anything to try to compensate for eating, like making yourself vomit or using laxatives?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had times where I ate a huge amount all at once, and I haven’t made myself throw up or used laxatives or anything like that. It’s more like I just haven’t been eating much or keeping track of meals.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, and if so, has this concerned you or changed how you feel about your body?

Yeah, I have lost weight. I don’t know the exact number, but my clothes are definitely looser, like hanging off me more than usual. At first I didn’t really care or even notice because I wasn’t eating real meals—just coffee and protein bars and not tracking anything. Now it does concern me a bit, because it feels like my eating just got away from me.
Have you been avoiding eating because you're not interested in food, or is it more about how you feel about your weight or body shape?

It’s more that I just stopped being interested in food and keeping up with it. I wasn’t really thinking about my weight or trying to change my body shape. I just stopped tracking meals, skipped real food for days, and was getting by on coffee and protein bars. Then my clothes started hanging loose before I really noticed.
Have you been worried about gaining weight or noticed changes in how you perceive your body shape during this time?

No, I wasn’t really worried about gaining weight or focused on my body shape. It was more like my eating just went off the rails—I stopped caring about tracking food, skipped real meals for days, and was mostly just having coffee and protein bars. Then I noticed my clothes were hanging loose, almost before I realized how little I’d been eating.

Have you noticed that your lack of interest in food is related to how you feel about your body or a fear of gaining weight, or does it seem more like a loss of appetite or disinterest that isn’t connected to your body image?

It seems more like loss of appetite or disinterest, not really about my body image. I came in because my eating just kind of went completely off the rails. I stopped caring about tracking food, skipped real meals for days, and was basically living on coffee and protein bars. Then my clothes started hanging loose before I even really noticed what was happening.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or energy levels around the same time that your eating habits changed?

Yeah, around that same time my mood and energy were way up. For days I felt like I was unstoppable, like I was brilliant and moving faster than everyone else. But I was also really irritable—if someone asked me a basic question or slowed me down, I’d snap at them like they were sabotaging everything at work.
How long did you feel that way—like you were unstoppable and moving faster than everyone else but also really irritable?
It was about three weeks, I think. It kind of built up over that time after I got handed that temporary PMO-level responsibility, and then it just kept ramping up.
During that time when you felt like you were unstoppable and moving faster than everyone else, did you also find that you needed less sleep than usual?

Yeah. I was barely sleeping—maybe two or three hours a night—and I’d wake up feeling charged, like I didn’t really need it. At the time it felt like sleep was just this inefficient thing I’d somehow gotten past.

During that time when you felt like you were moving faster and were more irritable, did you find yourself doing a lot more things during the day, like taking on extra projects or moving around a lot more than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I was doing way more than usual. I’d be building dashboards, rewriting timelines, sending out strategy notes, then at home I’d start reorganizing my apartment. I was also making new project templates all at once. It felt like I couldn’t sit still, like I had to keep moving from one thing to the next.
